comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: LAYER 1 CRATE-LEVEL MODULE MAP (the layer's phase-2a design act; attended, this session). Home: vsdd-core, beside the existing schema-bundle modules. NEW MODULES: (1) diagnostics.rs — the rustc-shaped Diagnostic both new modules emit: file, failure kind, location when the failure is a parse, message, recovery action (machine token) and recovery text (human) — kinds and recovery members LOADED from the statusline data set at runtime, never hardcoded, because the kind-to-action mapping is versioned data. (2) state/ — mod.rs public API (State, read_state -> Result<State, Diagnostic>, write_state with boundary evidence); schema.rs the State struct mirroring state-schema.md's state_fields verbatim (schema_version, nullable current_phase and current_layer with the pinned null meanings, open_findings_pointer, optional last_gate_result with the closed gate-kind enum, active_composition with config_inputs_hash, optional forward-only published); read.rs effectful read wrapping a PURE validate-bytes core — bootstrap self-validation gates on schema_version before further reads; the three read-failure kinds map exactly to statusline-data's enumeration, diagnostic-never-panic on every path; write.rs atomic write (temp-plus-rename, no partial file survives) with the PURE published-immutability check (a diff touching published after first write is refused) and the declared constraints re-checked at write. (3) registry/ — mod.rs load_all yielding the nine typed sets keyed by schema_class, each validated against its .mdatron/schemas pair at read via mdatron-core (the boundary: vsdd supplies schemas, mdatron executes; self-validation until the state-consistency family lands); frontmatter.rs PURE markdown-with-frontmatter extraction with parse-location capture; sets.rs one typed struct per schema_class, field names mirroring the artifacts. PURITY BOUNDARIES per the verification architecture: parse, validate, and the immutability check are pure over bytes and values — the property and mutation targets; file IO is effectful shell, integration-tested. TRUST BOUNDARY: state.yaml and the registry are adopter-edited — every read failure yields the diagnostic, never a panic. TEST SURFACE the red gate authors against: state read (happy, absent, malformed-with-location, permission-denied, future-schema-version refused, pinned null semantics), state write (atomicity under injected failure, published immutability, evidence required), registry (all nine load from the live tree; corrupted frontmatter diagnostic; class mismatch diagnostic), diagnostics (machine form carries the loaded tokens; human form rustc-shaped; every failure path returns).

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: TWO PROPOSALS FOR OPERATOR ADOPTION (agent-drafted candidates; proposals only until adoption is recorded, per The operator authors the oracle). PROPOSAL A — Layer 1 red-gate seed: (1) command binding: cargo test --workspace, AND the estate gap this drafting found: .crosslink/hook-config.json agent_test_commands is currently UNSET while gate-data's command_binding cites it as this estate's declared binding — the adoption sets agent_test_commands to cargo test --workspace, closing the citation; (2) baseline: the pre-implementation commit is the last phase-2a commit (stamped on this trail when suite authoring completes; the gate checks out that commit and runs the suite there); (3) expected red shape: every Layer 1 test fails EXECUTED — the suite compiles against stub API surfaces and tests fail at run time (kind: panic against unimplemented stubs, or assertion-failure where a partial behavior exists) — no compile-failure reds, honoring the executed-pin doctrine at layer scale; falsifiability is carried by each test's assertion content per the QE discipline; (4) flake policy: gate-data's 3 runs, kind-set aggregation; (5) zero pre-existing failures excused: the workspace suite is green today, so any red at baseline beyond the new tests is investigated, not waved through. PROPOSAL B — Layer 1 manual-test checklist (lands as manual-tests/layer-1.md on adoption; surface note: items drive the layer's fixture harness or the smallest reader entry point the layer lands — the operator may adjust surfaces at adoption): (1) malformed state file (drop a colon in .vsdd/state.yaml) — the diagnostic names the file, the parse location, and the restore-content recovery; no panic, no backtrace; (2) absent state file — worded diagnostic naming the path with the restore recovery; nonzero exit; (3) permission failure (chmod 000) — the permission-or-input/output diagnostic with the branched recovery text (permissions, or the disk or mount fault); (4) published-marker immutability — hand-edit a written published block; the next read flags it naming the field; (5) registry resilience — corrupt one registry artifact's frontmatter; its diagnostic names that file and location while the other eight load; (6) future schema_version — refusal names the version seen and the versions supported; (7) color-strip and assistive read — the failing cases in a no-color terminal lose no information, and the diagnostics read as complete sentences (the assistive-technology pass is the operator's checklist slot with a named reader, per the verification architecture); (8) token fidelity — one kind's machine token and recovery action spot-checked verbatim against templates/registry/statusline-data.md. Both proposals await the operator's adoption decision on this issue.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: OPERATOR ADOPTION (2026-07-21): both proposals adopted as presented. CORRECTION recorded with the adoption, per the provenance discipline: Proposal A claimed agent_test_commands was unset — false; the drafting probe read the wrong JSON level. The binding exists at agent_overrides.agent_test_commands = [cargo test], which at the workspace root already runs all members. Under the adopted text the value updates to cargo test --workspace — an explicitness alignment, not a gap closure; the false-gap claim does not stand. SEED, as adopted with that correction: command binding cargo test --workspace via agent_overrides.agent_test_commands; baseline = the last phase-2a commit, stamped on this trail at suite completion; expected red shape = every Layer 1 test fails EXECUTED against stub API surfaces (panic or assertion-failure kinds), no compile-failure reds; 3-run kind-set aggregation; zero pre-existing failures excused. CHECKLIST: lands as manual-tests/layer-1.md with this adoption cited. Red-gate authoring begins against the module map's declared API.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: DIVERGENCE NOTE, recorded once for the phase (the stated-reason rule): the chassis post-edit hook flags todo! bodies as stub patterns in the Layer 1 modules. Expected and correct during phase 2a — the todo! bodies ARE the red-gate pre-implementation surface: the API compiles, the tests execute and fail (panic kind, valid red), and 2b implementation turns them green. The contract's gate doctrine mandates this posture (tests never shown failing first are the assertion-based transition the gate blocks); where the ridden vehicle's generic conduct conflicts, the contract governs. The hook's warning stands as a useful tripwire OUTSIDE phase 2a; within it, this note is the recorded reason. Every todo! is tagged 2b and the phase-2b entry sweep clears them — a todo! surviving 2b's green gate is a real defect.
